fly

Footprints, selection and georeferencing for British Columbia’s historic airphotos.

fly helps you find and use British Columbia’s historic airphotos. The province’s catalogue records where each photo was taken, but not the ground it shows. fly works that out for most photos, finds the photos over your study area, picks a small set that covers as much of it as you need, and can download the photos and place them on a map.

Older photos often show a site before roads, farming and logging changed it. That makes them a reference for what to restore toward, and a baseline for measuring change.

With an elevation model, fly allows for the height of the land under the aircraft, which makes the footprints of film photos more accurate, and it corrects the errors it can identify in the catalogue’s flying heights.

The upper Bulkley River (Neexdzii Kwa) near McKilligan Road and Houston, BC, in 1971 and 1981, placed on the map by fly. Each photo sits on its own estimated footprint, so features line up approximately rather than exactly.

Installation 

pak::pak("NewGraphEnvironment/fly")

Functions still change between releases (NEWS), so pin a version for repeatable work: pak::pak("NewGraphEnvironment/fly@vX.Y.Z").

Example

Twenty 1968 photos of the Upper Bulkley River floodplain near Houston, BC, ship with the package. How much of the floodplain each scale covers, and the fewest photos that cover 80% of it:

library(fly)

centroids <- sf::st_read(system.file("testdata/photo_centroids.gpkg", package = "fly"), quiet = TRUE)
aoi <- sf::st_read(system.file("testdata/aoi.gpkg", package = "fly"), quiet = TRUE)

fly_coverage(centroids, aoi, by = "scale")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   scale   n_photos covered_km2 coverage_pct
#>   <chr>      <int>       <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1 1:12000       10        14.8         59.5
#> 2 1:31680       10        24.8        100

selected <- fly_select(centroids, aoi, mode = "minimal", target_coverage = 0.8)
#> Selecting photos (target: 80% coverage)...
#>   3 photos -> 81.6% coverage
#> Selected 3 of 20 photos for 81.6% coverage

From there, fly_fetch() downloads the photos’ thumbnails and fly_georef() writes each one as a GeoTIFF on its footprint.

Ecosystem

Package Role
fresh Stream network modelling engine: segment, classify, cluster, aggregate
link Intrinsic habitat models: develop, test and communicate
wet Stream flow and water temperature for BC’s Freshwater Atlas
flooded Delineate floodplain extents from DEMs and stream networks
drift Track land cover change within floodplains over time
floodplains Floodplain and land cover change modelling for BC watershed groups
stac_floodplains_bc STAC catalogue of floodplain land cover change in BC, 2017-2023, by watershed group
cd Climate departure analysis from ERA5-Land reanalysis
fly Estimate airphoto footprints and select photos that cover a study area (this package)
stac_airphoto_bc STAC catalogue of historic BC airphotos georeferenced with fly

Historic airphotos: fly (footprints, selection, georeferencing) → stac_airphoto_bc (published)

Data and methods it builds on

  • The province’s airphoto centroids in the BC Data Catalogue, with the thumbnails, flight logbooks, camera calibration reports and camera files the records link to.
  • NRCan’s MRDEM-30 elevation model, the one the height checks were measured against.
  • GDAL, through sf, for warping and masking the scans.
